Direction B — Blocks × Console — in both themes.

One component, two token sets. Every colour is a CSS custom property set on the root and read with var(), exactly as the real app does it: globals.css stamps data-theme on <html> and nothing below has to know which mode it is in.

The Theme chips above each artboard switch mode and accent independently — all four Hamdaz palettes work in both.

THE ONE RULE WORTH KNOWING

The selected row always breaks its surface. On dark it inverts to a white sheet; on light it inverts to an ink block. Same move, opposite direction — so the row that matters reads first without needing a border, a tint, or an accent bar.

The accent itself never changes value between modes. It is only ever a fill carrying dark ink, never body text, which is why it does not need a duller variant to stay legible.

WHAT CHANGES IN LIGHT

Nothing goes dark. The panels step in tone (grey ground, white blocks) and pick up a soft shadow where dark relied on the ground being darker than the block.

The record sheet becomes a tinted well rather than white-on-white, and the pink used for 'out of the pool' darkens — #ff4fa3 at 9px is unreadable on white, so light mode uses the darkened variant the same way globals.css derives --second-text.

BACKEND CHANGE, NOW SHOWN

The ranking used to score on open tasks. It now scores on ACTIVE tasks — not finished and the bid still open — with bid-closed and expired counted separately.

So the list column is Active, not Open, and the sheet's tiles carry Active / Bid closed / Overdue / Idle. Showing the wider open count next to the score made the order look wrong.
